subject: Clarification: SLA credit offsets and liability trigger mechanics (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Tanya Rivera <tanya.rivera@acme-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Fri, Apr 10, 2027 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Question on how SLA credits interact with liability cap in the draft MSA

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for walking us through the draft last week. Our legal team reviewed the MSA + Order Form and surfaced one open point that we need to close before legal can sign: the relationship between service credits (SLA) and the limitation of liability / sole remedy language.

Specifically: if an availability breach triggers credits, do credits reduce the customer's damages recovery under the cap (i.e., credits are an offset) or are they independent (i.e., credits are the sole remedy and the liability cap still applies to other damages)? Our counsel flags two concerns: (1) if credits are an offset, they want clear mechanics for calculating the offset and timing; (2) if credits are sole remedy, they want an express carve-out for willful misconduct and IP infringement.

We attached our redlines to the Order Form and a short spreadsheet showing sample calculations. Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether your team can accept the proposed carve-outs for the IP/willful-misconduct exception?

Next step: would it make sense to do a 30-minute legal sync early next week? We can include our GC.

Thanks,
Tanya Rivera
Head of Procurement
Acme Analytics

Attachments: ACME_redlines_v2.docx (Order Form redlines), SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx (sample offsets)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tanya Rivera <tanya.rivera@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, Apr 10, 2027 at 10:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Question on how SLA credits interact with liability cap in the draft MSA

Tanya —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Short answer: Redwood prefers that service credits be the exclusive remedy for SLA breaches (i.e., credits are the sole remedy for service-level failures), but we anticipate negotiating narrow carve-outs for statutory claims and proven willful misconduct. Credits are not typically treated as an offset against other damages in our standard MSA.

However, I understand how your legal team would prefer either an offset mechanism or a detailed calculation to avoid double recovery concerns. To move quickly, I propose the following options for discussion during a short legal call:

- Option A (Redwood default): SLA credits = sole and exclusive remedy for availability/latency SLO failures; liability cap remains in place for other claims; carve-outs for IP, willful misconduct, gross negligence.
- Option B (Compromise): SLA credits reduce any monetary recovery for the same incident up to the credit amount; parties agree a short timetable (30 days) for finalizing credit calculations and credits paid in the next billing cycle.
- Option C (Customer-first): Credits are independent safeguards (no offset), but Redwood increases the credit cap for the first 12 months or provides a one-time service credit pool for migration period.

I copied Dev and Marissa to quickly confirm whether Dev's team can produce the calculation language (Option B mechanics) and if Marissa can review escalation/fallback language from the order form.

Happy to join a 30-minute legal sync. I'm free Monday 4/13 08:30-10:00 or Tuesday 4/14 14:00-16:00 PDT.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Question on how SLA credits interact with liability cap in the draft MSA

On Fri, Apr 10, 2027 at 10:03 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Tanya —
> 
> Appreciate the clear summary and the redlines. Short answer: Redwood prefers that service credits be the exclusive remedy for SLA breaches...

Tanya / Olga / team —

Following up from the options Olga outlined. From an implementation and auditing perspective, Option B (credits as offsets with clear calculation rules) is manageable if we can agree on a deterministic formula and evidence exchange. Proposed mechanics below for the Order Form redline:

- Trigger: a sustained availability event where measured uptime for a calendar day is below 99.5% as measured by Redwood monitoring.
- Calculation window: allocate affected requests by customer token/session id where feasible; default to percentage-of-impacted-requests if per-request mapping is impractical.
- Credit amount: pro-rated monthly fee * outage percentage (simple: outage% * monthly committed spend).
- Offset rule: any monetary damages claimed for the same incident are reduced by credits already paid or payable; timing: credits applied to next invoice; if a refund is requested, credit applied within 30 days.

We can add a short evidence section requiring both parties to exchange logs (retention scope limited to 90 days) and an escalation path to an impartial engineer review. That gives your counsel something auditable and limits the scope for disagreements.

One caveat from our side: we need to keep the IP and willful-misconduct carve-outs explicit and preserved (we can't accept claims for third-party data misuse broadly).

If this approach looks reasonable, I can draft a redline paragraph for the Order Form (Option B mechanics) and circulate.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Sr. Product Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tanya Rivera <tanya.rivera@acme-analytics.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, Apr 18, 2027 at 04:45 PM PDT
Subject: Final proposal: Operational offsets + narrow carve-outs (redline attached)

Tanya / Counsel / Olga —

Thanks for the productive thread and for the clear spreadsheet. We've discussed internally (legal + product + sales ops) and propose the following narrowly-scoped compromise. Please see attached redline (ACME_redlines_v2.docx) with tracked changes. High-level summary:

1) SLA credits remain the exclusive remedy for service-level breaches, except where the claim arises from willful misconduct, gross negligence, or IP infringement (these remain carve-outs to the sole remedy).
2) For operational clarity, credits will be treated as an offset against monetary damages for the identical incident where the customer seeks additional monetary relief. The offset mechanics are limited: credits actually paid or payable for that incident within 60 days of the incident date will be deducted from any monetary award.
3) Credit calculation: pro-rated committed monthly fee multiplied by the percentage outage for the billing period; evidence exchange window = 30 days; logs retained for 90 days.
4) One-time migration protection: for the first 90 days after go-live, Redwood will increase the maximum monthly credit cap to 50% of committed monthly fees (instead of standard 25%) to provide extra runway during migration.

Next steps: If Acme legal can review and confirm the redline, we'll prepare an amendment to the Order Form for signature. If you prefer, we can also sign off a short MOU capturing the credit mechanics while finalizing language in the MSA.

Olga: let's set a short call with Acme GC tomorrow to close lingering wording. I'm available 9:00-11:00 PDT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Partnerships & Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: ACME_redlines_v2.docx (proposed language), SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx (updated sample with migration protection)

Governing notes: this redline keeps the cap language unchanged but documents a narrow offset mechanism and a limited migration credit uplift.
